steps.name: An epic sized by the portfolio default renders hatched
steps.description:
One production file: `Lighthouse.Frontend/src/components/Common/Charts/DeliveryEpicSizeChart.tsx`. Everything else in the slice already exists — slice 02 records and parses `isUsingDefaultSize`, and the demo seed already flips Heat Shield Testing from true to false on elapsed day 9.

FOLLOW ADR-119 AS REVISED (2026-08-02), NOT AS ORIGINALLY WRITTEN. The series split is withdrawn: keep ONE bar series per epic, keyed on `referenceId`, exactly as slice 02 ships it. Slice 02's scenarios assert those ids and their ordering and must stay green.

Four changes:

(1) Build a per-epic-per-day estimate lookup beside the existing size lookup. `sizesOn(point)` already walks a day's `featureBreakdown`; add the parallel map from `referenceId` to that day's `isUsingDefaultSize`. AC-3.5 is load-bearing: `null` and absent BOTH mean actual. Only an explicit `true` is a guess. Every snapshot recorded before slice 02 has no flag at all, so reading absence as `true` would render the entire back-history hatched.

(2) Emit an SVG `<pattern>` definition once per chart instance, with an id derived from React's `useId()`. AC-3.6: two deliveries can be expanded on the same page at once, and a hardcoded id would make the second chart reuse the first's def. Put the `<defs>` inside the ChartsContainer children so it lands in the same SVG as the bars that reference it.

(3) Pass `slots={{ bar: ... }}` to `ChartsContainer`. The renderer takes `ownerState` and returns the bar element, filling with `url(#hatch-{instanceId})` when `estimatedByEpicDay[seriesId]?.[dataIndex]` is true and with `ownerState.color` otherwise. `BarElementOwnerState` is `{ seriesId, dataIndex, color, isFaded, isHighlighted, isFocused }` — verified against @mui/x-charts@9.0.1 in ADR-119. The DISTILL scenarios call this slot DIRECTLY with a synthetic `{ seriesId, dataIndex }`, render whatever it returns inside an `<svg>`, and read the `fill` attribute off the first `rect` or `path`, so the returned element must carry `fill` as an attribute rather than only as a CSS class.

(4) Extend each bar series' `valueFormatter` so a hatched day's tooltip says the size is a default. It currently formats null as null (which is what keeps an absent epic out of the day's tooltip — do not break that) and a number as a plain string. Add the default-size wording for a day whose flag is true. AC-3.3: the solid segment's tooltip must NOT carry that wording. The scenario matches /default/i, so the exact phrasing is yours — DISCUSS suggested 'size is the portfolio default (not broken down)'.

Then run the full frontend gate and report the dogfood state; the maintainer runs the visual check.

steps.implementation_notes:
MOCK-SURFACE COUPLING, the trap this feature has already paid for twice. The test mocks `@mui/x-charts` with exactly EIGHT named exports: ChartsContainer, BarPlot, LinePlot, MarkPlot, ChartsXAxis, ChartsYAxis, ChartsTooltip, ChartsLegend. Importing a ninth name from that barrel resolves to `undefined` and React throws on render, breaking every scenario in the file at once; a deep-path import bypasses the mock entirely. The pattern def needs no import — `<defs>` and `<pattern>` are plain SVG elements.

The hatch must read against EVERY epic colour, since `getColorMapForKeys` spreads epics across a green-teal ramp. Diagonal strokes in a colour derived from the segment's own fill (a lighter or darker variant) survive that better than a fixed white or black, which disappears on one end of the ramp. The maintainer checks this on the demo instance in both light and dark mode — the count line needed exactly this treatment one review ago.

The demo seed needs NO change. `DemoDataService` already carries `HeatShieldBreakdownElapsedDay = 9` with `HeatShieldSizeByElapsedDay` flat at 30 through day 8 then 18 from day 9, and the flag flips with it. That is the flip the screenshot for the docs page will be taken from.

CI learnings apply (docs/ci-learnings.md — read before writing). Frontend-side, `typescript:S7735` (negated condition in a ternary) is what this kind of flag handling invites most; `S3776` if the renderer grows branches.

maintainer_decisions: ADR-119's series split is withdrawn (2026-08-02, Benjamin). One series per epic; the renderer keys on seriesId AND dataIndex. Rationale is in the ADR's Revision section — chiefly that the split makes the null-twin tooltip bug the steady state, rewrites slice 02's green assertions, and doubles what slice 04's legend filter must de-duplicate.
No legend in this slice either. It lands in slice 04, collapsed by default, together with the fever chart's.
out_of_scope: Any recorder, DTO or parser change — the flag already flows end to end from slice 02
The docs page and its @screenshot — owed at feature finalization, taken from the seeded flip
